purpose: The single machine-readable registry of what is true, what is contested, and what is ours. A coherence critic uses this file to tell a DELIBERATE in-world contradiction from a MISTAKE. If a contradiction is not in here, it is a mistake.

tier_definitions.hard-canon: Stated repeatedly and consistently across shipped Bethesda/ZOS material. The authorial world model obeys it. An in-world speaker may doubt it; narration may not.
tier_definitions.soft-canon: Stated once, or only by an unreliable in-world source, or era-scoped. We may take a side; the side must be registered.
tier_definitions.apocryphal: From a source the series itself marks unreliable. An in-world OPINION, never narration.
tier_definitions.constructed: Our invention. Binding on this project once written. Contradicting it is as much a failure as contradicting Bethesda.

provenance_definitions.community-data: Verified this session against a community-wiki summary returned by search. SECOND-HAND: a summary of a wiki summary of primary in-game text. Cite and re-verify when possible.
provenance_definitions.canonical-recall: Recalled from direct play/reading of the shipped games. Unverified.

verification_note: Direct fetches to en.uesp.net, elderscrolls.fandom.com, imperial-library.info and lagbt.wiwiland.net were all refused (HTTP 403 at the agent proxy gateway) on 2026-08-05. All 'community-data' entries rest on search-result summaries. An agent with unblocked access should re-verify CF-025, CF-044 and CF-050 before wave 2.

field_schema.id: CF-nnn hard/soft canon | CF-Dnnn disputed | CF-Cnnn constructed
field_schema.in_world_sources: books/NPCs in OUR game that assert this
field_schema.positions: [{id, in_world_source, stance, held_by[]}] — required when disputed
field_schema.deliberately_open: boolean — true means NO answer exists; never resolve it
field_schema.contradicts_ok: may our fiction contradict this? false = never
field_schema.dispute_kind: fact | judgment — only `fact` disputes belong in this registry; see `not_disputes`
field_schema.topics: dialogue topic ids this dispute is argued on, resolved against the build at boot
field_schema.holders: {actors[], factions[], races[], settlements[]} — the machine half of `held_by`. game/src/world/canon.js#stanceOf reads it; races and settlements NARROW an actor/faction match and are never a stance on their own.
field_schema.voiced_by: book:<id> | dialogue:<topic>#<actor> | npc:<id> — shipped sources that actually say this. Resolved against the build at boot; a dangle throws.
field_schema.when: {era, year, ends, note} — where a fact sits in the province's history. `year: null` with a note is a first-class answer: several of the oldest facts are undated IN WORLD and saying so is the fact.

facts.claim: The Hist are giant sentient spore-trees native to Black Marsh, growing chiefly in the interior swamps.
sources_real: Pocket Guide to the Empire 3rd ed., Argonia

facts.claim: Argonian hatchlings drink Hist sap at hatching; the sap confers the hatchling's soul.
facts.notes: Load-bearing for the entire souls-as-levelling diegesis (RI-LOR05).

facts.claim: When an Argonian dies its soul returns to its Hist, is held there, and may be issued again to a later hatchling.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Hist (snippet): 'Argonian souls return to the Hist after death... the sap becomes the Argonian's blood, essence, and soul'
facts.notes: THE most load-bearing canon fact in this corpus. Bethesda built a souls-and-respawn metaphysics into Black Marsh and never made a game of it.

facts.claim: The Hist shapes Argonian bodies, deciding what hatches, and can reshape Argonians to meet need.
sources_real: Recurrent in ESO Murkmire and UESP Lore:Argonian
facts.notes: Anchor for levelling-as-regrowth. Because the Hist edits bodies, levelling is broad (attributes), not a score.

facts.claim: Hist sap carries the Hist's communication — visions, warning, summons — to an Argonian who drinks or licks it.
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Ledger (the flood anecdote)

facts.claim: Hist sap consumed by a NON-Argonian is a hallucinogen causing bloodlust; the drinker does not perceive what they are killing.
sources_real: Oblivion quest 'Infiltration'; UESP Lore:Blackwood Company (snippets) — the Water's Edge massacre
in_world_sources: A Practical Handling of the Marsh-Fevers, section 10
facts.notes: The entire sap-taint system rests on this. Softening it into a stat malus wastes hard canon.

facts.claim: Hist sap increases the combat prowess of those who drink it; Argonian shamans use it ritually.
The Hist say the Void is 'where all roots lead' and that they rejoin it; they speak of invoking the 'Songs of Sithis' in vengeance.
facts.notes: Attributed to the Hist THEMSELVES — in-world testimony, not narration.

facts.claim: During the Oblivion Crisis (3E 433+) the Hist withdrew the Argonians and organised a counter-invasion of the Deadlands so ferocious that Dagon's lieutenants sealed the gates.
facts.notes: AFTER our era. Never referenced in game. Establishes only that the Hist can act at continental scale when it chooses.

facts.claim: Argonians are reptilian, breathe water, and resist disease.
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin

facts.claim: Jel is the Argonian root-tongue; it runs on idiom and metaphor, is near-untranslatable without Black Marsh cultural knowledge, and forms words chiefly by compounding.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Jel; The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer (snippets)

facts.claim: Argonians carry both Jel names and Tamrielic names, the latter often direct translations of the former.
Hyphenated Tamrielic Argonian names may encode gender through the possessive (Lifts-Her-Tail, Hides-His-Eyes).
Attested Jel roots include beeko (friend), deelith (teacher), ku-vastei (needed change), xanmeer (stone-nest), lukiul (assimilated Argonian), kaoc (curse), thtithil (egg).
sources_real: The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer; UESP Lore:Shadowscales; UESP Lore:Ixtaxh Xanmeer (snippets)
facts.notes: RE-VERIFY FIRST. Glosses came from summaries, not the primer's own text.

facts.claim: The Naga are a scaled, serpentine Argonian form. Imperial sources characterise them as thugs responsible for banditry.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Naga; Pocket Guide 3rd ed. ('Argonian "Naga" thugs') (snippets)
facts.notes: The EXISTENCE of the Naga is hard canon; the 'thug' characterisation is Imperial contempt and must be depicted as such, never voiced as narration.

facts.claim: Argonians born under the sign of the Shadow are taken at birth and given to the Dark Brotherhood as Shadowscales; survivors to adulthood become full members.
Shadowscales may leave the Brotherhood to serve Black Marsh as ku-vastei — agents of needed change and arbiters who act with impunity.
facts.notes: A ready-made quest-giving institution with zero invention cost.

facts.claim: Duskfall ended the ancient high Argonian civilisation; the knowledge of how the xanmeers were built was lost with it and no living Argonian has it.

when.note: The Duskfall. Undated in every in-world source and deliberately so: no book in this build gives it a year, and the three that try give three different spans.

facts.claim: Xanmeers ('stone-nests') are pre-Duskfall Argonian stepped ziggurats, often in symmetrical complexes joined by elevated stone walkways, carved with geometric patterns and images of the ancient Argonians. Many are sunken or buried.

when.note: The xanmeers were raised before the Duskfall, over an interval the chronology does not attempt.

facts.claim: Many xanmeers are shrines erected in both reverence to and fear of Sithis; the purpose of many is lost.
facts.notes: Direct anchor for CF-C010, the soul-reservoir below the Stone Wastes.

when.note: Same horizon as CF-041. Argued in-world as CF-D007.

facts.claim: Xanmeer names are Jel compounds, e.g. Ixtaxh-Thitithil-Meht ≈ 'Exact Egg-Cracker'.
The Ruddy Man is a figure of ancient Black Marsh legend associated with the deep past and a stone or ruddy body.
sources_real: UNVERIFIED — search this session returned no corroboration
facts.notes: DO NOT build load-bearing plot on this until verified. Low confidence; may be misremembered.

when.note: The Ruddy Man belongs to the same undated horizon and is the only figure in it with a name.

facts.claim: The Knahaten Flu began at Stormhold in 2E 560 and persisted 41 years, to 2E 601.

when.note: The Knahaten Flu. The one deep-time event in this registry with a real date, and the only pre-Third-Era year that appears anywhere in the shipped tree.

facts.claim: The Knahaten Flu drove the Kothringi and the Lilmothiit to extinction; Argonians were unaffected.
The Kothringi were silver-skinned humans native to Black Marsh, of Nedic descent, and notable sailors.
A small number of Kothringi survived the Flu 'through unnatural means'.
facts.notes: OPEN HOOK: one living Kothringi in 3E 427 is canon-legal and exactly the kind of impossible person Morrowind would have placed.

facts.claim: Blackrose prison was built by Potentate Versidae-Shae on the ruins of a Lilmothiit settlement called Blackrose.
sources_real: Partial corroboration in search snippet; primary source unverified
facts.notes: RE-VERIFY.

facts.claim: The Empire holds the coasts of Black Marsh and uses the interior for prisons; the heart of the province remains solely Argonian and is not under Imperial control.
sources_real: Pocket Guide to the Empire 3rd ed., Argonia (snippet)

when.note: The present arrangement. The harbour agreements that produced it span roughly a century and no source gives a year for any of them.

facts.claim: House Dres of Morrowind has raided Black Marsh for slaves for centuries and slavery remains legal in Morrowind in 3E 427.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Black Marsh; Morrowind (3E 427) (snippets + shipped game)
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin
The Blessings of the Coast (denies it)
facts.notes: The era's central grievance. Must be depicted as CURRENT, never as history.

when.note: House Dres has raided for centuries; no in-world source in this build dates the first raid.

facts.claim: The Blackwood Company is a Leyawiin mercenary outfit, chiefly Khajiit and Argonian, that secretly doses its members with sap from a Hist kept in its hall cellar.
The An-Xileel formed during the Oblivion Crisis (3E 433+) and therefore DO NOT EXIST in 3E 427.
facts.notes: MOST LIKELY CANON BREAK. A builder searching 'Argonian faction' finds the wiki page and uses it. Naming them is an automatic 0.

facts.claim: REJECTED SOURCE: claims that Gideon is 'ruled by a Root-Assembly' and Blackrose 'governed by a Warden-Brood' originate from an AI-generated worldbuilding site (fables.gg), not from canon.
sources_real: fables.gg — REJECTED, non-canonical, do not re-import
facts.notes: Logged so no later agent re-imports it. Fluent, confident, entirely fabricated — the exact failure mode this registry exists to catch, encountered on day one.

facts.claim: Binding place names from the project map: Lilmoth, Soulrest, Blackrose, Gideon, Stormhold, Thorn, Archon, Helstrom; regions Valus Ridge, Blackwood, The Hive, Marauder's Coast, Stone Wastes, Western Rootlands, Eastern Rootlands, The Deep Marshes, The Stone Forest, The Clay Moor, Crimson Coast; waters Topal Bay, Padomaic Ocean.
facts.notes: No builder may rename, respell or 'improve' these. Helstrom is rendered on the map in an uncial face where H reads as b.

facts.claim: The interior of Black Marsh is functionally impassable to outsiders — no roads, shifting water, disease, and navigation by knowledge no foreigner has.
sources_real: Pocket Guide 3rd ed.; project map (tracks terminate at the coasts)
in_world_sources: A Practical Handling of the Marsh-Fevers

facts.claim: What survives when an Argonian soul returns to the Hist?
sources_real: Canon establishes the return (CF-003) but never adjudicates what persists.

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Ledger (Sergius Verrent)
positions.stance: The sap is a solvent. The individual dissolves into a common stock; what is issued to a new egg is MADE OF the dead, as a second loaf is made of the same flour. Argonians have no life after this one, only a contribution.

positions.in_world_source: The Egg Speaks Twice (Third Song)
positions.stance: The tree gives him out again; that is the whole promise. The question 'is it the same person' is a foreign question the language does not contain.

facts.authorially_true: partial:The PATTERN survives; the MEMORY does not. Verent is right that nothing individual is recalled and wrong that nothing individual persists. The root-song is right that the promise was never memory. NEITHER source is corrected in game, and the third position — that WELLS remember what the tree forgets — is voiced only by drunks and by the Drowned Court.

facts.claim: Who cut the first sapwell, and why?
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Ledger (records only that rootkeepers refuse to say)

positions.in_world_source: oral tradition, Helstrom
positions.stance: The Hist cut itself, and the keepers only keep the cut open.

positions.in_world_source: Drowned Court commonplace book
positions.stance: The Kothringi cut the first, and the Knahaten Flu was the payment.

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Ledger
positions.stance: Nobody will say, and they become genuinely angry when pressed.

facts.notes: NO ANSWER EXISTS. Do not resolve this in any quest, book or ending. A future writer WILL want to; this flag is the refusal.

facts.claim: Were the xanmeers built by Argonians, or built by someone older and merely occupied by them?
in_world_sources: An Imperial antiquarian's survey (T1, to be written)

positions.in_world_source: Imperial antiquarian survey
positions.stance: The present Argonians cannot build such things and never could; the xanmeers are the work of a vanished people whose ruins the natives inherited.

positions.in_world_source: The Egg Speaks Twice (Seventh Song)
positions.stance: 'Our grandmothers stacked the world into steps and walked up it. We do not know how.'

facts.authorially_true: B
facts.notes: B matches hard canon CF-040/CF-041. Position A is a WRONG view held by real NPCs, and its wrongness is racial condescension. A critic must not flag A as an error — it is registered.

facts.claim: Is the Hist one mind or many trees?

positions.in_world_source: Imperial usage
positions.stance: 'The Hist' is a species. Trees are individuals, like any grove.

positions.in_world_source: rootkeepers of Helstrom
positions.stance: There is one tree. What you see are its fingers.

positions.in_world_source: the Lilmoth keepers
positions.stance: There was one. Some fingers have stopped listening.

facts.authorially_true: C
facts.notes: Our resolution, chosen because canon uses both singular and plural and never adjudicates (CF-008). C preserves both usages and is the only one that leaves room for CF-009's rogue trees.

facts.claim: What caused the Knahaten Flu?
sources_real: UESP Lore:Knahaten Flu (snippet): one account blames an Argonian shaman who manipulated the spore-trees in revenge; another attributes it to natural causes. Canon does not adjudicate.
in_world_sources: An Imperial history (T7, to be written)

positions.in_world_source: Imperial history
positions.stance: An Argonian shaman engineered it through a manipulation of the Hist, in revenge for the treatment of his people.

positions.in_world_source: Argonian oral account
positions.stance: Natural. The marsh is full of fevers and this one travelled.

facts.authorially_true: partial:It was Hist-borne but not authored by any single person. Position A's slander is that it names a culprit; position B's evasion is that it denies the tree's involvement. NEITHER is corrected in game.
facts.notes: CANON ITSELF leaves this contradiction standing. It is the proof-of-convention for this whole registry.

facts.claim: Why has the Rootward Tide begun to fail?

positions.in_world_source: Deep-Kin testimony
positions.stance: Root-theft. The soul-gem trade intercepts the fall. Foreigners are drinking the marsh.

positions.in_world_source: Wet Ledger commissioned survey
positions.stance: Too many wounds. Thirty years of Sap-Cutters opening wells for sale; the tree is bleeding capacity.

positions.in_world_source: Drowned Court burial ledgers
positions.stance: It started before the cutting and before the gem trade. Something below the Stone Wastes is filling.

facts.authorially_true: C
facts.notes: A and B must be given GENUINELY GOOD evidence — both are real aggravations, and a player who acts on either does real good and fixes nothing. See CF-C010.

facts.claim: Legion strength in Black Marsh in 3E 427 is thin because reserves were redeployed to the Vvardenfell crisis.
In 3E 427 the Blackwood Company is a young Leyawiin outfit operating in Black Marsh, hunting for a Hist to take. It has not yet acquired the tree it is documented as holding in 3E 433.
facts.notes: Canon-compatible prequel to CF-064. Canon states no founding date (CF-065).

facts.claim: In 3E 427 there is an isolationist current in the interior — the Xul-Aneekh, 'the Deep-Kin' — a consensus, not a party, from which An-Xileel sentiment later grows. They are NEVER called the An-Xileel.
The Wet Ledger is a compact of lukiul river-factors and Imperial merchants controlling Gideon's tolls, warehouses and the Governor's debts.
The Ixtu-Vakh (Sap-Cutters) are Argonian heretics who cut sapwells for profit and sell hist-sap phials to foreigners.
The Drowned Court of Soulrest is a mixed-race mortuary order, four centuries old, that buries or burns the dead of every people for a fee.

when.note: The Drowned Court, four centuries old at 3E 427.

facts.claim: The Blackrose Prefect runs a labour-lease scheme renting prisoners to coastal plantations and, through intermediaries, to Dres factors. Legal on paper; slavery in fact.

The Rootward Tide: everything that dies in Black Marsh leaks soul-stuff downward into a water table threaded with Hist root, which drinks it and holds it as pattern (eixa). Sap is soul in liquid form; Jel has one word, vei, for blood and sap.
facts.notes: In-world this is an Argonian IDIOM, not established Tamrielic scholarship. No foreign scholar may state it as settled.

facts.claim: A sapwell (ixtu-xul) is a Hist root deliberately cut and kept open. Wells remember what the tree forgets, because a wound is a place where something happened. This is why a well can re-issue a specific person.
facts.notes: The single constructed claim the entire checkpoint system rests on. In-world it is voiced only by drunks (per The Sap and the Ledger) and by the Drowned Court.

facts.claim: Beneath the Stone Wastes near Soulrest, a pre-Duskfall xanmeer engine built to HOLD souls is filling. It is the true cause of the Tide's failure — and the sapwells work because of it.
facts.notes: BINDING AND SECRET. No NPC may state this before the registered discovery point. Anchored in CF-042 (xanmeers as shrines in reverence and fear of Sithis). Resolving it should be able to switch off respawning — a Morrowind quest decision reaching into a Souls mechanic.

facts.claim: Sap-taint (teekh-kaoc): a non-Argonian who rests at sapwells accumulates corruption in five bands, ending in the Hist addressing them directly. At band 3 enemy SKINS lie; frames, hitboxes, telegraphs, damage and AI never change.
facts.notes: Derives directly from hard canon CF-006. Altering combat behaviour under taint is an AR-1 automatic fail.

facts.claim: Travel is by poled barge along Hist-advised routes: a poler asks the tree each morning which way the water moved in the night. Purchasable with gold, schedule-bound, refusable, severable as a plot event. Sapwells never teleport.
facts.notes: Satisfies ARBITRATION seam S7.

facts.claim: Xul-hesh (root-theft): soul-gem trapping intercepts soul-stuff that would have gone down to the roots. Argonians regard it as somewhere between poisoning a well and kidnapping, and its Daedric patron is Molag Bal.
facts.notes: Molag Bal's patronage of soul gems is canon; the Argonian reading of the trade is ours.

facts.claim: The year 3E 427 is known in interior Argonian reckoning as the Ninth Sap-Fall since the Rootless Egg. Interior Argonians count by the Hist's cycle, not the Imperial calendar.
facts.notes: An NPC who gives you an Imperial date is telling you something about themselves.

when.note: The present. Interior reckoning: the Ninth Sap-Fall since the Rootless Egg.

facts.claim: What was the house under the Stone Wastes built to do?
in_world_sources: Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Reverence
Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Fear

positions.in_world_source: Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Reverence (Ojal-Weeth, of the Drowned Court)
positions.stance: It was raised to hold and to honour, and the burying that goes on above it now is the same act continued.

positions.in_world_source: Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Fear (Undersexton Bel Mourne)
positions.stance: It was raised to keep something where it was put, and every feature she can measure is a feature for keeping in.
held_by: the undersextons who keep the current leaves
Imperial antiquarians who have read her

facts.authorially_true: partial:Neither author is describing the building. Both reason from the habits of people four hundred years and one culture downstream of whoever laid the floor, and the floor was laid for a third reason neither has considered.
facts.notes: Registered by W1-23 from a shipped pair that was carrying `cf: CF-042` — a fact that is not marked disputed and has no positions. The books were arguing and the registry could not tell a reader so.

facts.claim: Are subjects of the Empire held as property in this province?
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin, Salt-Factor
Marginalia, in a borrowed copy of the Blessings of the Coast

positions.in_world_source: The Blessings of the Coast: An Address to the Free Peoples of Argonia
positions.stance: No subject of the Empire may be held as property within the borders of the Empire's law. Where it has happened it has happened beyond that law, at the hands of foreign vessels.
held_by: most officers of the Ninth on the coast

positions.in_world_source: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin, Salt-Factor; and the marginalia in a borrowed copy of the Blessings
positions.stance: Morrowind is in the Empire and Tear is in Morrowind. The House enters people in the stock column and takes them out of it, and the only thing the law changes is which word the paper uses.
held_by: the underwriters of the Wet Ledger
every soul who has been on the Blackrose roll
the second hand in the margin

positions.stance: It is not answered in sight of that building. Whoever asks there is asking on the record, and the record is not this one's to bring home.
held_by: Argonians of the townside quarters, when an Imperial or Provincial building is in view
anyone questioned about it within sight of the Assize or the Office

facts.authorially_true: partial: B is what a book-keeper's audit finds — the House's stock column is the operative fact and the law's word does not reach it. But B is silent on its own terms about whether the roll ever lets go and about who is safe to ask, and both turn out to matter more than the book-keeping. See CF-D028 for the first and C for the second.
facts.notes: The province's central moral fact, and it had no registry entry. The two books carried `cf: CF-062`, which records that the Empire abolished slavery in most of Tamriel — true, and not the thing they disagree about. The ruling is B and is sealed out of the shipped build; nothing in the game says so.

facts.claim: Does the labour-lease at Blackrose raise any question of consent?
in_world_sources: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volumes the Second and Third

positions.in_world_source: Of the Labour-Lease at Blackrose, and Why It Is Not What You Have Been Told (Prefect Galvus Arn)
positions.stance: A prisoner under sentence works; that is the sentence. Every difficulty in the arrangement is a difficulty about counting, and there is no other kind.
held_by: the clerks who draw the instruments

positions.in_world_source: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volumes the Second and Third
positions.stance: It arises, it has always arisen, and the reason neither Arn nor the bench raised it is that it did not occur to either of them that there was a question. The mark on the paper is the mark of a woman answering a different one.
held_by: the interior, who have said it from the start
junior clerks who have stopped saying it out loud

facts.authorially_true: B
facts.notes: Distinct from CF-D008 on purpose: D008 is about what a person IS under the law, D009 about what a signature MEANS. A court can hold A on Monday and B on Friday without noticing, and the Casebook is the record of one doing exactly that over three volumes.

facts.claim: Why does the Empire not hold the interior of this province?
in_world_sources: A Short Account of the Pacification of the Argonian Coast
The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volume the Third

positions.in_world_source: The Blessings of the Coast
positions.stance: Because it does not wish to. The Empire does not go where it is not wanted, and the address says so proudly.
held_by: the address as it was published at the chartered markets

positions.in_world_source: A Short Account of the Pacification of the Argonian Coast (Tribune Vell)
positions.stance: Because a charter requires a signatory and the interior does not produce them. The province was contracted for, harbour by harbour, and inland there was nobody to contract with.
held_by: every serjeant who has been asked to try

positions.in_world_source: The Account the Marsh Keeps; and the Casebook, Volume the Third
positions.stance: Because it was refused. Courteously, for an afternoon at a time, on behalf of no office, in a manner that cannot be appealed — and the difference between "no signatory" and "a refusal you cannot file" is the whole province.
held_by: the judge at Gideon in his last volume

facts.authorially_true: C
facts.notes: Reframed by W1-23 after reading the books. The three texts AGREE on the fact — the Legion does not go inland — and the interesting disagreement is about the cause, which is where the province's politics actually live. Consistent with CF-C001 (the thin Legion), which states the fact and takes no view on why.

facts.claim: What happened to the relief column at Reman's Ford?
in_world_sources: A Short Account of the Pacification
The Relief of the Reman Ford
The Water Does Not Take Sides
On the Drowning at the Ford
Nine Stanzas Upon the Drowning of Reman's Ford

positions.in_world_source: A Short Account of the Pacification (Tribune Vell), issued to every officer at the schools
positions.stance: A flood surge. No enemy, no engagement, an accident of water in a province where water has accidents. Two hundred at muster and forty-nine at the far bank.
held_by: most of the Cohort's own officers

positions.in_world_source: The Relief of the Reman Ford, assembled from the Cohort's own papers
positions.stance: There was a fight before the water came. The day-books at Gideon say so, Vell never read them, and the province will not admit it.
held_by: the prefect at Gideon who wrote it
the officers who have read the day-books

positions.in_world_source: The Water Does Not Take Sides; and On the Drowning at the Ford
positions.stance: The gates were opened, by our people, and nothing else was done. Thirty at the weirs against two hundred with iron on could not have fought and did not try.
held_by: the weir families above the ford
the villages that keep the lifting

positions.in_world_source: Nine Stanzas Upon the Drowning of Reman's Ford
positions.stance: More was done than the gates, and by hands the poem names and the record does not.
held_by: the depot men who will not have it sung

facts.authorially_true: partial:The gates were opened deliberately and there was no engagement. Vell is right that no enemy fought and wrong that it was an accident. The prefect has found men who died with wounds and has not considered that a column drowning in armour in a weir race wounds itself. The song is a song.
facts.notes: Five shipped books argue this, across four positions, and every one of the edges between them carried no `cf` or a `cf` naming a fact rather than a dispute. It is the province's founding grievance and it was the largest unregistered contradiction in the build.

when.note: Reman's Ford. Dated in the shipped books and the only dated event any registered dispute turns on.

facts.claim: Has the Drowned Tally ever had a ninth clause?
in_world_sources: The Seventh Recension of the Drowned Tally
That the Ninth Clause Is Old
On the Ninth Clause, and What Was Done to the Fair Copies

positions.in_world_source: That the Ninth Clause Is Old: An Answer to the Archive
positions.stance: It is old. The fair copies the archive holds were made after it was struck, which is precisely why they do not carry it.
held_by: the scribes of the eleventh volume

positions.in_world_source: The Seventh Recension, entire; and On the Ninth Clause, and What Was Done to the Fair Copies
positions.stance: The Recension is entire and it has eight. A clause nobody can produce is a clause nobody wrote.

facts.authorially_true: partial:There was a ninth and it was never struck, because it was never written. The clause is a thing the Court does and not a thing the Court has. Both sides are arguing about a document and the document was never where it lived.
facts.notes: Three shipped books, four edges, no `cf` on any of them.

facts.claim: Has the Drowned Court's unit of return drifted between the sixth volume and the eleventh?

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Tally, Sixth Volume: the disputed leaves, with the archive's note
positions.stance: The unit is what it has always been. The disputed leaves are a copying error and the archive said so at the time.

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Tally, Eleventh Volume: the current leaves
positions.stance: A return of four is an ordinary return on this coast and has been for as long as either of us has been a sexton. Two of us drew together and got the same. The measure is not at fault.
held_by: the sextons keeping the current leaves

facts.authorially_true: partial:Both volumes are counted correctly. They are not counting the same thing, and neither house has ever asked the other what it means by a return.
facts.notes: Registered at `confidence: medium`: the arithmetic is authored across three books by two pieces and has not been reconciled leaf by leaf.

facts.claim: Did the Drowned Court confirm that eleven burial boxes came up carrying nothing?
in_world_sources: The Soulrest Sheet, for the week of the ninth

positions.in_world_source: The Soulrest Sheet, for the week of the ninth
positions.stance: The Court has confirmed it, an undersexton found the weight in person, and readers will draw their own conclusions.
held_by: the Soulrest sheet and its readers

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Tally, Eleventh Volume: the current leaves
positions.stance: Nothing of the kind is entered. A sexton speaking in a yard is not the Court, and the Court speaks in the volume or it has not spoken.
held_by: the sextons keeping the current leaves

facts.authorially_true: partial:The weight was found and the confirmation was never given. A sexton said it in a yard, a printer set the word CONFIRMED over it, and the volume is right that nothing was entered.
facts.notes: Registered as a dispute about what a Court SAID, not about what was in the boxes. What was in them is not this registry's business and no position here touches it.

facts.claim: Do the stone nests have chambers inside them?
in_world_sources: The Stone Nests of Argonia, Volume the First
A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third

positions.in_world_source: The Stone Nests of Argonia, Volume the First: A Survey of Eleven Sites
positions.stance: The mass is solid and the proportion is constant. What visitors take for chambers are collapse voids and robbers' cuts, and he has measured eleven sites with the same rod.
held_by: anyone who has read the survey and not been inside one

positions.in_world_source: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third
positions.stance: There are chambers, and he stood in one, and he will not be told otherwise by a man who measured the outside.
held_by: the guides who take travellers in
the people who sell what is in them

facts.authorially_true: partial:Both men are right about the site each of them stood at. The proportion is constant and the interior is not, and Rethan's eleven sites do not include the two that are hollow.

facts.claim: What happens at a drinking?
in_world_sources: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third

positions.in_world_source: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third
positions.stance: A ceremony, observed from the bank by a gentleman with a notebook, and reported in the terms a gentleman had available.
held_by: the Provincial Office's file on the interior

positions.in_world_source: The Egg Speaks Twice: Nine Root-Songs of the Deep Marshes (First Song, Of the Drinking)
positions.stance: Before the drinking you were water. The tree put its finger in the water and the water stood up, and the word for that is not in the visitor's language and is not "birth".
held_by: anyone who has been at one

facts.authorially_true: partial:The visitor's description of what was done is accurate and his account of what it was is not, and the singer says in his own preface that the crossing cannot be made in Tamrielic. Neither text is corrected and neither could be.

facts.claim: May a sapwell be cut for sale at all, under the old terms?
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Knife: the Old Terms of Cutting
What the Hollow Has to Trade

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Knife: the Old Terms of Cutting
positions.stance: Everyone argues whether, and whether is not in the terms. The terms are depth and season, they are four hundred years old, and a cut made to them is lawful whoever buys it.
held_by: the cutters who were taught the three places
the hollows that have nothing else

positions.in_world_source: the keepers who taught the three places, against the man who wrote them down
positions.stance: The terms are silent on selling because selling was unthinkable, and a silence is not a permission. Writing the three places into one book is itself the offence.
held_by: the keepers who taught him and have stopped speaking to him

facts.authorially_true: partial:The terms are silent and the silence is not a permission, and it is also not a prohibition, and four hundred years of it not mattering is why nobody wrote the sentence that would settle it.
facts.notes: The shipped edge pairs `the-sap-and-the-knife` with `what-the-hollow-has-to-trade`, but those two texts are on the SAME side — a cutter's manual and a hollow with nothing else to sell, both arguing that the question is how and not whether. The dispute is real and the other party is the keepers, who are voiced in dialogue and had no book. Registered with both texts under A.

facts.claim: Are the notched stones on the third terrace Imperial boundary stones?
in_world_sources: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volume the First
On the Tally-Stones of the Blackwood

positions.in_world_source: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volume the First: Of the Forms
positions.stance: They are boundary stones. The court has taken them as such in evidence, which is what a boundary stone is.
held_by: the holders whose claims rest on them

positions.in_world_source: On the Tally-Stones of the Blackwood, with a Note on Their Ornament (Aurelia Sitte)
positions.stance: They are tallies. Every measurement in her paper is correct and she counted the notches before she decided what they were, which is the wrong order and gets the right count.
held_by: the Office's expenses clerk, who paid for it
the rootkeepers, for entirely different reasons

facts.authorially_true: partial:They are neither, and they were standing before there was a boundary to mark or an Office to mark it, and both readings are a later use of an older object.

facts.claim: Were the long reaping blades weapons before the Duskfall, or farm tools picked up in a bad year?
in_world_sources: A Letter to Teeus-Ahai, Who Should Have Asked Somebody Who Cuts Rice

positions.in_world_source: The Reaper and the Scythe: On the Long Curved Blades
positions.stance: They were carried in the Duskfall. The rice came to them afterwards, the way rice comes to everything here.
held_by: the men who teach the long curved blade

positions.in_world_source: A Letter to Teeus-Ahai, Who Should Have Asked Somebody Who Cuts Rice
positions.stance: It is a harvest edge. It went to war in a bad year the way a boat-hook does, and anyone who has cut a season could have said so.
held_by: the rice villages of the Blackwood

facts.authorially_true: partial:The blade is a farm tool and the grip is not. Somebody in the Duskfall put a soldier's handle on a harvester's edge, and each author is describing the half of the object he has held.
facts.notes: The one martial edge that is a disagreement about a FACT rather than about what is worth doing. See `not_disputes` for the four that are not.

facts.claim: In what order do the landmarks of the Topal shore run actually stand?
in_world_sources: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Second
The Topal Shore Run, as it is Actually Sailed

positions.in_world_source: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Second
positions.stance: The order given in the Progress, taken from the deck of a hired boat on one passage in fair weather.
held_by: travellers who buy the Progress before they arrive

positions.in_world_source: The Topal Shore Run, as it is Actually Sailed
positions.stance: The order the pilots keep, which differs because two of the marks move with the season and one of them is not there any more.

facts.authorially_true: B
facts.notes: Kept, against RI-LOR06 "How we lose" #8, because it is PERCEIVABLE: a player who walks or sails the shore can settle it without being told. A dispute the player can check is texture; a dispute over a date they can never reach is a typo with a schema.

facts.claim: Is sight in this province a competence the country takes away, or the wrong sense to have trained on?
in_world_sources: Notes on the Employment of Destructive Magic in This Province
Not Being Seen in a Country That Has No Shadows

positions.in_world_source: Notes on the Employment of Destructive Magic in This Province (Battle-Mage Tertius Ollo)
positions.stance: A trained man can put a spell into a body at eighty paces and this country takes that away from him, and there is no substitute for it. The fault is the province's.

positions.in_world_source: Not Being Seen in a Country That Has No Shadows (Uxith-Ei, hunter at the Thornmarsh edge)
positions.stance: The eye was never the sense to train. You are hidden from the water, the reeds, the birds and your own smell, and a person taught properly here is not working round a defect.
held_by: the hunters of the Thornmarsh edge

facts.authorially_true: B
facts.notes: Registered by W1-23 roughly four minutes after the pair landed on disk, mid-wave, from another piece still writing. That is the finding, not the fact: with no gate, the registry falls out of date with the shipped tree within MINUTES on a busy tree. tools/lore/canon-census.mjs should run in the same place check-content does.

facts.claim: This build has no Argonian tribes. The province is organised by four constructed bodies — the Deep-Kin, the Drowned Court, the Wet Ledger and the Xul-Aneekh — and by the rootkeepers.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Argonian tribes (Agacephs, Paatru, Archein, Sarpa, Dead-Water, Miredancers)
facts.measured: Counted over all of game/data on 2026-08-07 (W1-23 r2; supersedes the earlier count this same fact shipped with, taken before the tribes piece landed): Deep-Kin 87, Xul-Aneekh 84, Drowned Court 64, Sap-Cutters 53, Wet Ledger 45. Of the tribes canon actually names, all six now score non-zero after the tribes piece: Agacephs 53, Paatru 34, Archein 50, Sarpa 26, Dead-Water 10, Miredancers 47. Kothringi 22 and Lilmothiit 4 remain extinct in-world (history, not population); Horwalli remains 1. "Naga" scores 388 but is a playable race in this build, not a tribe.
facts.notes: Registered so the omission is a DECISION on the record rather than a gap. It is defensible — four bodies a player can tell apart beat nine tribe names they cannot — but it is ours, it is not canon, and the failure mode it guards against is a later agent scattering canonical tribe names through dialogue as texture and thereby claiming a social structure this world does not model. If tribes are wanted, they need a faction each, not a mention each. W1-23 r2: the mention became a faction record — see game/data/factions/ — closing the half of this note the tribes piece had not yet reached. tools/lore/canon-census.mjs now re-checks this field against the live tree so a future re-count cannot go stale unnoticed the way this one did for a wave.

facts.claim: In this build the slave trade is present chiefly as the Empire's euphemism for it. The word "lease" outnumbers the word "slave" by roughly fifty to one.
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin
facts.measured: Counted over all of game/data on 2026-08-07: lease/Blackrose 2,240 hits; House Dres 245; slave/slavery 42; soul-gem or soul trade 15.
facts.notes: This is an effect worth having and a risk worth naming. CF-062 is hard canon: House Dres has raided Black Marsh for slaves for centuries and slavery is legal in Morrowind. A province that only ever says "lease" has adopted the Provincial Office's vocabulary as narration, which is precisely the move RI-LOR06 §1.2 forbids at the authorial level. The correction is not to add the word everywhere; it is that the euphemism must be somebody's POSITION and not the world's voice, which is why CF-D008 exists and why the Blessings of the Coast is registered as holding it rather than stating it.

facts.claim: Does the soul of an Argonian who dies far from his own Hist reach it?

positions.in_world_source: The Grange Book (Archein Weighs-The-Rains)
positions.stance: Distance is nothing to a root. A man who dies at Tear is home before the letter is, and the tree is no poorer for the journey.
held_by: most of the Provincial Office by inheritance

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: The nearest root still awake takes what it can reach. It is not his tree. He is issued out again a stranger, and the tree that made him is short by one in that year's count.
held_by: the Miredancers of the Eastern Rootlands

positions.in_world_source: Told at the Weir (Ranaso Quick-Tally, under-factor)
positions.stance: Distance costs. What comes back comes back short, the ground where he fell goes heavy, and there is no unit for how short.
held_by: the Agacephs of the Deep Marshes
the Naga-Kur, who carry their dead home at a price they pay in the open

facts.authorially_true: partial: reach is not a distance, it is whether a root at the far end is still listening, so B has the mechanism right and is wrong to file the stranger as a loss. C is right that a cost is paid and wrong about what pays it: the heaviness in the ground is real and it is not the man. A is simply wrong, and A is the position that makes the lease bearable to the people who write it.
facts.notes: The dispute the province's central euphemism rests on. If A is true, sending a leased man to Tear costs him nothing, and every Archein in Blackwood has an answer for the question the Casebook raises about consent. Nothing in the build states the ruling and no book adjudicates. Does not contradict CF-003, which states that the soul returns to its Hist and says nothing about the Hist's reach.

facts.claim: Is the tree behind the wall on the Gideon estates a Hist of its own, or a cutting?

positions.in_world_source: The Grange Book (Archein Weighs-The-Rains)
positions.stance: Ours, and older than the Office. Entered on the survey as a Hist and tithed as a Hist. The wall went up over theft and not over shame.
held_by: the rootkeepers who have inspected it and signed

positions.in_world_source: Told at the Weir (Ranaso Quick-Tally, under-factor)
positions.stance: A cutting, carried off the Rootlands in a wet sack and put in a hole. It grows and it drinks and it holds nothing. The water under it runs clear, and clear means the root is going sideways.
held_by: most of the interior when the subject comes up

positions.in_world_source: Sap-Speaker Neekh-Otei, and the Miredancer elders with her
positions.stance: A true tree that has stopped answering, which is a third thing and worse than either of the other two.
held_by: the Sap-Speaker, who would rather it were a cutting

facts.authorially_true: C
facts.notes: Ruling C. The estate tree is real and it has gone quiet, which is the Rootward Tide arriving at the one family in the province that has an accountant. Position A is a wrong view held by people with a survey, a tithe receipt and four generations of eggs under the tree, and a critic must not flag it as an error.

facts.claim: Is a hatchling given the sap from a vessel, away from the tree, given a soul?

positions.in_world_source: The Grange Book (Archein Weighs-The-Rains)
positions.stance: Sap is sap. Same tree, same hatchling, and the vessel is a vessel. The yard is also safer than the root, and half a wild hatching goes into the water.
held_by: the estate-hatched, who are the argument's own evidence

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: The tree must be over it, with the roots under it, and it must see. What comes out of a cup is a body with something borrowed in it, and a loan has a term.
held_by: the Agacephs, who put it in one sentence and will not argue past it

positions.in_world_source: The burial figures of the Drowned Court at Soulrest
positions.stance: They get a soul and they come back short. The Court has the figures and the figures run four hundred years: estate-hatched and cup-given die a little young and bury a little heavy.
held_by: the sextons at Soulrest who keep the ledgers

facts.authorially_true: partial: the sap carries it and the tree's sight is not required, so A has the mechanism right. C has the figures right and the cause wrong — the estate-hatched die young because the estates work them young, and the Court has never separated the two. B is wrong, and it is the only one of the three whose holders would abandon it if they were shown the numbers, which is why they are never shown the numbers.
facts.notes: The class question and the metaphysics in one object. Does not contradict CF-002, which states that the hatchling drinks Hist sap at hatching and does not state where the drinking must happen. The Drowned Court position is held by faction alone, so an Imperial notary who happens to share the `archivist` actor is offered nothing — the narrowest live demonstration in the build that the register gates by who somebody is and not by what job they do.

facts.claim: Was the Duskfall one night, or generations?
in_world_sources: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior

when.note: Undated in every in-world source and deliberately so. The dispute is about the SHAPE of the event, not its date, and no position here supplies a year.

positions.in_world_source: Xeeth of the Stone Forest, and the Sarpa generally
positions.stance: One night. Every stepped ruin in the province went over the same way, north-east shoulder first, and that can only be seen from the air.
held_by: one Imperial surveyor who has written it down and not published it

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: Generations. The tablets change hand three times inside the falling, and a hand changes when a person dies.
held_by: the Sap-Speakers, who hold the tablets

positions.in_world_source: The Paatru of the Clay Moor
positions.stance: Three burnings, not one. The clay carries three black seams with clean clay between them, at the same depths anywhere on the moor.
held_by: anyone who has dug a pit on the Clay Moor in the dry season

facts.authorially_true: partial: three burnings across two long lifetimes. C counts the fires and B counts the writing and they are counting different things, so both are right and neither will say so. A is wrong about the night and right about the shoulder — the ruins did all go the same way, because they were all raised to the same alignment, and nothing that fell chose a direction.
facts.notes: One of the two pre-Duskfall disputes this piece exists to add. W1-23 §5 measured 21 named years in the shipped build and zero outside the Third Era; this is a disagreement about an event no faction in the province is old enough to have argued about at the time. No position supplies a date and the ruling does not either. The pressure to answer it never goes away — RI-LOR06 check 6 applies here as much as to CF-D002.

facts.claim: Does the bone a Dead-Water warrior wears hold the dead back from the root?
sources_real: Tribes of Murkmire: The Dead-Water Tribe — the Naga-Kur adorn weapons and armour with the faces, claws and bones of fallen comrades, and hold that it lets them fight after death

positions.in_world_source: Dead-Water Koor-Nakh, at the Thorn gate
positions.stance: It holds her here and she fights. The shield turned twice and I was there for both.

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Court at Soulrest
positions.stance: The pattern left at the moment of death. A bone is a bone after that — good bone, honoured bone, still bone. The Court has looked, professionally, for four hundred years.

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: Nothing in the bone, and the going is delayed while the bone is above ground, and the delay is paid at the far end by somebody who was not asked.
held_by: the Sap-Speaker, who says it once and does not say it twice

facts.authorially_true: partial: nothing is in the bone and the delay is real, so B is right about the bone and wrong to conclude from that that no cost is paid. C holds both halves and has the cost in the wrong column — it comes off the tree's count for the year, not off a particular hatchling. A is wrong, and the shield turned twice.
facts.notes: The practice is canon (Tribes of Murkmire: The Dead-Water Tribe). What the practice DOES is not, and canon has never asked. Position A is held by a people who have paid for it in the open and will keep paying, and a critic must not read their sincerity as an error.

facts.claim: What were the elevated stone walkways between the xanmeers built for?
sources_real: Lore:Xanmeer — xanmeers often stand in symmetrical complexes joined by elevated stone walkways (CF-041). Canon does not say what the walkways were for.
in_world_sources: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior

when.note: Built before the Duskfall by builders whose method is lost (CF-040). Every position here is an inference from wear, from a level, or from a memory nobody can date.

positions.in_world_source: Xeeth of the Stone Forest, and the Sarpa generally
positions.stance: Roosts. A hand and a half wide, running where no foot needs to go, worn on the outer edge where a claw sits. We were up there.

positions.in_world_source: Told at the Weir (Ranaso Quick-Tally, under-factor)
positions.stance: Roads. Door to door, with kerbs, and steps at both ends. Nothing flew.
held_by: every interior guide who has walked one

positions.in_world_source: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior (Decius Arral, antiquarian)
positions.stance: Aqueducts. Eight runs measured with a level and a cord, each falling one part in four hundred along its whole length. A road does not need a fall.
held_by: the Gideon court, on Arral's authority and without reading him

facts.authorially_true: partial: water first and feet afterwards. Arral's fall is a real measurement taken correctly and the kerbs are a real kerb, and the Agacephs walked the dry channels for four hundred years after the water stopped. The wear on the outer edge is Sarpa wear and is centuries younger than the stone it is on.
facts.notes: The second pre-Duskfall dispute, and the one a player can settle without being told: walk a high walk, look at what wore it, and look for the fall. RI-LOR06 §8 warns against disputes the player cannot perceive; this is the answer to that warning rather than an exception to it. Nothing in the game states the ruling.

facts.claim: Does the lease-roll ever release the person entered on it, or is the entry hereditary and permanent?

positions.stance: The roll does not come off. I have watched it move from a mother to her daughter, and nothing on the paper says different.
held_by: the cutters of the Ixtu-Vakh yards
most who have been on the roll longer than ten years

positions.stance: It came off a man on the number-four gang, once, eleven winters back, bought clear for silver that took his whole house to raise. Bought is not free. It is also not never.
held_by: a handful who have bought clear, and those who knew them

facts.authorially_true: partial: both witnesses are right about what they saw. Manumission happens — rarely, and priced to keep it rare — so "never" and "not never" are both true depending which side of the price a person is standing on. The operating reality for almost everyone on the roll is permanence; the exception is real and is not a refutation of it.
facts.notes: Voiced by dialogue alone, on purpose: this is oral testimony from two people the province does not let write books. Registered so the answer to CF-D008 is not the only thing the roll is ever asked about — a fact can be property and still have its own separate, disputed shape.

facts.claim: The Agacephs of the Deep Marshes will not chase an animal, will not eat one that was chased, keep no sapwell, and will not give a direction — they take you, and you still do not learn the way.
facts.notes: Ours. Canon (The Argonian Account, Book 4) gives the Agacephs as an interior people near the Hist who find little in the outside world worth seeing, and gives their rescue of Decumus Scotti. The diet, the absence of a sapwell and the refusal to give directions are RI-LOR08 §2.1 and are ours. The refusal is the reason the Wet Ledger has no chart of the interior.

facts.claim: The Paatru of the Clay Moor kill strangers in the wet season, because the clay holds the year's eggs; in the dry they trade at the moor's edge. They eat eggs that did not take, buried in clay. Their Hist is in a pit and they go down to it on a rope. They will not cross another people's bridge and they take nobody in.
facts.notes: Ours. Canon (The Argonian Account, Book 4) gives the toad-like Paatru as an interior people who would have killed an outsider on sight. The SEASON is ours, and it is the whole of the invention: canon supplies the hostility and no reason for it, and a law with a calendar is a different thing from a temper. Two Paatru are on the Blackrose roll and both were taken at the trade-edge in the dry, which the roll has no column for.

facts.claim: The Sarpa of the Stone Forest eat carrion, keep a Hist that is a stump and say the true tree is overhead, weigh Imperial coin and drop it, and will not come down into a place they have not been asked into. They have seen every xanmeer in the province from above.
facts.notes: Ours. Canon (The Argonian Account, Book 4) gives the winged Sarpa as an interior people hostile to strangers. The stump, the carrion, the refusal to land uninvited and the aerial survey are ours. The last is load-bearing: it makes the Sarpa the only witness to the shape of the deep past and makes them the witness nobody has ever questioned. RI-LOR08 'How we lose' #7 — the Sarpa are not a mount and not a race option.

facts.claim: The Archein keep an estate Hist behind a wall and bring hatchlings sap in a copper cup; they eat Imperial food in courses from a written menu; they deal through a factor and never at the quay, and hold that distinction to be the whole of their honour.
facts.notes: Ours, on a canon foundation that is unusually solid. The Pocket Guide 3rd ed. makes the Archeins the Empire's native governors of the rural province; The Argonian Account Bk 4 calls them slaver kleptocrats; ESO's From Argonian to Saxhleel puts them in the employ of House Dres; Bk 3's Archein Right-Foot-Rock sells a she-worker's newborn twins to a trader in town. The wall, the cup, the menu and the factor rule are ours. The factor rule is the mechanism by which a chain of custody becomes a chain of clean hands, and it is the answer to the finding that this build says `lease` fifty times for every `slave` — RI-LOR08 §5.

facts.claim: The Miredancers name a Sap-Speaker who descends to the roots or the canopy, is fed only by the tree, and pays for it in gold tongue and bark-scale. The eighteenth Speaker has descended four times and brought back nothing, and will descend again.
facts.notes: The office, the descent, the diet of sap and the symptoms are canon (Tribes of Murkmire: Miredancers; Lore:Hist Sap), carried forward from 2E 582 on the argument that the sources present the office as ancient. The FOUR EMPTY DESCENTS are ours, and they are the Rootward Tide (CF-C008) at the scale of one person rather than one institution. Whether she should keep drinking is an argument and is deliberately not registered as a dispute — nobody disagrees about any fact of it.

facts.claim: The Dead-Water keep no Hist and drink at whichever tree they are nearest to; they take from other Argonian villages and are forgiven; they will not leave a body under any conditions; and it is they, not the weather, who close the tracks around Thorn.
facts.notes: The Naga-Kur, the bone practice and the fear they are held in are canon (Tribes of Murkmire: The Dead-Water Tribe). The visiting of other peoples' trees, the absolute refusal to leave a body, and the identification of the Dead-Water as the hand behind the closed tracks at Thorn are ours. The last one connects an existing shipped plot beat — RI-LOR02: 'when Thorn falls silent, the interior has decided something' — to somebody who decides.

not_disputes.what_this_is: Contradiction edges declared between shipped books that were EXAMINED and ruled not to be contradictions. RI-LOR06 §1 admits two categories, registered or bug; this is the ruling that an edge is in neither, because the two texts are not disagreeing about a fact of the world. Recorded so the finding is durable and the same edges are not re-litigated every wave. `tools/lore/canon-census.mjs` reads this list and stops reporting them.
not_disputes.rule: A contradiction is a disagreement about what is the case. A disagreement about what is worth doing, what is fit, or what a man ought to carry is an ARGUMENT, and the province should be full of them. Registering an argument as a contradiction is how a registry fills with forty entries a player cannot perceive (RI-LOR06 "How we lose" #8), and it also destroys the registry's actual job, which is telling a critic a mistake from a design.

entries.on: whether a shield that cannot parry is worth carrying
entries.reason: Worth. Both texts agree on the fact — the great shields of the stone nests cannot turn a blow aside — and disagree about whether that settles the question of carrying one. Neither is wrong about the world.

entries.on: whether the high grip on the ricasso is worth the reach it gives up
entries.reason: Worth, and an explicit trade: both authors state the same exchange and price it differently. That is two schools, which RI-LOR03 asks for.

entries.on: whether a hooked weapon is fit for a soldier
entries.reason: Fitness. An uncle and a nephew disagreeing about what a soldier ought to carry. No fact of the province is at stake and the letters are better for it.

entries.on: whether the shield line may be opened in standing water
entries.reason: Not a contradiction at all: it is a regulation against a practice. The Standing Instruction states correctly what the Instruction says; Serjeant Brell states correctly what the men do. Both are true and the gap between them is the subject.

entries.on: whether a well may be cut for sale at all
entries.reason: The edge is MIS-DECLARED. Read together, the two texts agree: the cutter's manual says the terms are depth and season and that "whether" is not in them, and the hollow with one well and nothing else to trade is arguing the same case from the other end. Neither denies what the other asserts. The real opponent is the keepers, who hold that a silence is not a permission, and who had no book — so the dispute is registered as CF-D017 with BOTH of these texts under position A and the keepers voiced in dialogue.

truth_seal_salt_note: W1-23 r2. Folded into every truth_seal so a bare-letter ruling ("A"/"B"/"C") cannot be recovered by hashing the position ids the shipped file already publishes — see tools/lore/build-canon.mjs. Never shipped: project() builds its own top-level object and does not copy this one.
